messages:
Alex: Heads-up — found a reproducible OOM in the Android sample app that happens after a device rotation. It only shows up when the AuthInterceptor retries a 401. Steps: login, rotate, hit /user/profile -> app OOMs.

Maria: Ugh. Can you paste the stacktrace and the interceptor code? Also which okhttp/retrofit versions?

Alex: okhttp 4.11.0, retrofit 2.9.0, targetSdk 31. Stacktrace (trimmed):
```
FATAL EXCEPTION: main
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Failed to allocate a 65544 byte allocation with 41920 free bytes and 40KB until OOM
  at android.app.ActivityThread.performResumeActivity(ActivityThread.java:4658)
  at com.example.sample.MainActivity.onResume(MainActivity.kt:72)
  at android.app.Activity.performResume(Activity.java:8101)
  ...
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Activity leaked: com.example.sample.MainActivity@3f2a5c7
  at com.example.sample.AuthInterceptor.intercept(AuthInterceptor.kt:34)
```

Alex: Interceptor code simplified: 
```
class AuthInterceptor(private val tokenProvider: TokenProvider): Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val req = chain.request()
    val token = tokenProvider.token
    val withAuth = req.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $token").build()
    val resp = chain.proceed(withAuth)
    if (resp.code == 401) {
      // naive refresh + retry
      synchronized(this) { tokenProvider.refreshIfNeeded() }
      val retryReq = withAuth.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer ${tokenProvider.token}").build()
      return chain.proceed(retryReq)
    }
    return resp
  }
}
```

Alex: TokenProvider is a small helper that was created in MainActivity for the sample to show login UI (it holds an Activity reference to show a dialog). So the interceptor ends up keeping a ref to the Activity indirectly. Rotation -> Activity destroyed but still referenced by in-flight okhttp request -> leak -> OOM after repeated rotations.

Kevin: That explains it. We shouldn't capture Activity in any networking singleton. TokenProvider must use ApplicationContext or be lifecycle scoped. Also Auth interceptors retrying 401s manually is fragile.

Maria: Two quick fixes: 1) stop putting UI/context into TokenProvider (use ApplicationContext + send an event to UI via LiveData) 2) prefer OkHttp Authenticator for 401 handling — it receives the route and request and is designed to produce follow-up requests without leaking.

Jordan: Re: retry loop — also check that you don't call chain.proceed on the same response body after consuming it. That can cause weird behavior. And set `okHttpClient.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` for the sample while debugging to avoid network retries masking the bug.

Alex: Good call. I switched TokenProvider to use Application context and moved the dialog trigger to an activity-observed event. Also replaced the manual retry with an Authenticator:
```
class TokenAuthenticator(private val tokenStore: TokenStore): Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    if (responseCount(response) >= 2) return null // give up
    val newToken = tokenStore.refreshBlocking() ?: return null
    return response.request.newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken")
      .build()
  }
  private fun responseCount(response: Response): Int {
    var res: Response? = response
    var result = 1
    while (res?.priorResponse != null) {
      result++
      res = res.priorResponse
    }
    return result
  }
}
```

Lina: Nice. Authenticator avoids the interceptor keeping extra state across requests. Also the `responseCount` guard is important to avoid infinite retry storms.

CI-Bot: FYI the sampleapp CI caught a flake earlier — related to leaked activity memory after rotation on Firebase Test Lab. Linked run: https://ci.redwood/xyz/12345

Kevin: One more thing — document this pattern in devx onboarding: "Don't stash Activity/Context in network singletons; prefer Application context; use Authenticator for token refresh; cap retries." People keep making the same mistake in sample apps.

Alex: I'll open a PR to update the sample repo + add a short note in the SDK README about interceptor vs authenticator and the context/leak pitfall. Patch will: make TokenStore app-scoped, switch sample to Authenticator, set retryOnConnectionFailure(false) in debug build, and add unit test that simulates rotation by nulling activity ref.

Maria: Awesome — thanks. If you want I can review the PR and add a small e2e on Robolectric to validate no activity references remain. :thumbsup:

Alex: Please do. I'll ping when PR is up.

Jordan: And maybe we should add a lint rule or a devex checklist: "networking objects must not retain Activity/Fragment references" — low effort, high ROI.

Alex: Agreed. Will add issue to the devex backlog.

Lina: Great catch — this one will save other teams headaches. :tada:
